decisions.reason: The connector inventory and BOOT button are established by separate clauses in the same message; selecting the exact ESP32-S3 module does not change them.
The GPIO assignments were already revised for WROOM-1 availability before this event, and the N16R8 variant selection does not entail another pin reassignment.
The USB-C programming role is established independently in the same message; the exact module variant does not change the existing USB data-line or programming-port requirements.
The standalone LDO supply already covers the ESP32-S3 and complete 3.3V rail, and the exact module variant does not entail a change to its regulator, activation, or source-selection rules.
The boost enable GPIO was already changed to GPIO5 for WROOM-1 compatibility, and selecting the N16R8 variant does not change the boost-control behavior.
The DCDC1 rail already powers the ESP32-S3 as part of its load coverage, and the source does not change the rail voltage, rating, or load requirements.
The exact ESP32-S3 module variant does not alter the established I2C pull-up, series-resistor, cable-length, or bus-speed requirements.
The LED power, level shifting, data GPIO, and standby-control requirements remain unchanged by the exact ESP32-S3 module selection.
The source confirms that sensors remain on another board, which is consistent with the dedicated sensor-board fanout and does not change its current state.
The AXP2101 remains the normal power source for all system loads; selecting the exact ESP32-S3 module does not change the battery or system power path.
The ESP32-S3 module variant has no entailed effect on the battery protection controller, cutoff thresholds, or DW01A protection details.
The module selection does not change the J_BAT NTC connection or AXP2101 thermal-protection requirements.
